translation_notes: Every read of the region is translated, not only the five `g.value` calls: `tb.value(IRI[..], SEM.classCode / SEM.sectionNumber)` (x2, G2) and `g.value(o, p)` / `g.value(o, OWL.versionInfo)` / `g.value(o, OWL.versionIRI)` (G7) -> `m{ {..} .. ?v }.first()`; `tb.subject_objects(p)` -> `m{ ?s {p} ?o }` (the predicate is data, `sem:{k}` for k in EC.REL_PROPS); `list(g.subjects(RDF.type, OWL.Ontology))` -> `list(m{ ?s rdf:type owl:Ontology })`. `@graph tb` before G2/G3; `@graph g` as the first line of the loop body (re-evaluated at each iteration, so it follows the loop variable).

`@prefix sem: <...> as SEM .` instead of dropping `SEM = Namespace(...)`: SEM is a module-level value that the original defines and the harness compares (module-state oracle), and `as SEM` keeps that object while the reads use the prefix. `or ""` is the original's own default (`str(tb.value(..) or "")`), kept after `.first()` -- not a replacement for `default=`.

Context restored (shim semtech_gates_ctx.py + stand-ins): `HERE` is the script's data directory (/home/claude/semtech-landscape in the real script), here the region's own directory; `load`, the `nodes`/`secnum` numbering loop and `cls_iri` come from the real script (lines before the region) and are copied verbatim into the shim; the two tooling modules the script `load`s (07-tooling/taxonomy_v1_0_0.py, enrichment_c_v2_0_0.py) and the six TTL files it parses are small stand-ins in the example directory (the real ones are 55 KB / 17 KB / 530 KB of data), same shapes and vocabulary.

Why the driver wraps `rdflib.Graph.triples` (in the driver process, before the sides fork): the excerpt keeps only the lines that touch RDF, so `bad` is re-assigned five times and only the last value survives in the module globals; G2's and G3's results leave no trace except `edges`/`sem_classes`. Each side prints every pattern asked and every triple yielded, and stdout is compared. `g.value`'s first-value-only behaviour shows too: a class with two classCode values prints a single 'got'. Five inputs (shipped, clean, empty, multi-first = the two classCode values in the other order, falsy = header values ""/0/false), each in a scratch copy of the directory. Mutation checks: sem:sectionNumber -> sem:classCode, and `.first()` -> `.one()` on versionInfo, both made `rdfeval check` FAIL; restored.
optimization_notes: The region is the G7 header loop alone (source lines 114-121); the G2/G3 lines before it are context and belong to the extracted header, left byte for byte (translated.ldpy's islands there included).

optimized.py is identical to original.py: the loop is already in the script's dense one-line-if style. Every read must stay a value() read, because the driver logs every Graph.triples pattern and every triple consumed, and the `not g.value(o, p)` test is a truthiness test (a falsy "" or 0 counts as missing) that an `in` test would not reproduce.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: the Ontology subjects are `list(m{ ?s a owl:Ontology }(g))` (no per-iteration @graph needed); versionInfo/versionIRI keep `g.value(o, owl:...)` with prefixed names, and `g.value(o, p)` has no RDF term to rewrite.

Rule 4: `m{ {o} owl:versionInfo ?v }(g).first()` is 5 tokens longer than `g.value(o, owl:versionInfo)`, so the three value reads translated.ldpy turned into m{ }.first() go back to value(). `g.subjects(rdf:type, owl:Ontology)` and the m{ } have the same token count; the m{ } is kept because it needs no rdf: prefix.
header_optimization_notes: Python: URIRef, Literal, SKOS and XSD go; DCTERMS, OWL, RDF and RDFS (used by the context lines and the loop) join the rdflib import.

LD Python: Namespace, URIRef, Literal and the whole rdflib.namespace import go (the context and the loop use prefixed names; SEM comes from `@prefix sem: ... as SEM`), so only Graph is left; `@prefix rdf:` goes (the loop pattern uses `a`); sem:, rdfs:, owl: and dcterms: stay for the context lines.
